title: Chicken and Waffles for the Crew
subtitle: Crispy buttermilk fried chicken on Belgian waffles with maple butter.
description: Crispy chicken tenders with Belgian waffles on a platter — sweet, salty, and big enough for a crew that earned a splurge breakfast.

ingredients.name: buttermilk
ingredients.notes: for brine, plus 1 cup for dredge

ingredients.name: all-purpose flour
ingredients.notes: seasoned with salt, pepper, paprika, garlic powder

steps.title: Brine the chicken
steps.instruction: Soak chicken thighs in buttermilk with a tablespoon of salt for at least 30 minutes (or overnight). Remove from fridge 20 minutes before frying so pieces cook evenly.

steps.title: Mix waffle batter
steps.instruction: Prepare Belgian waffle batter per package directions using milk and melted butter. Rest batter 10 minutes while oil heats so starch hydrates and waffles stay crisp outside.

steps.title: Fry the chicken
steps.instruction: Heat oil in a heavy Dutch oven to 350°F on a thermometer. Dredge chicken in seasoned flour, shake off excess, and fry in batches 12–14 minutes until golden and internal temperature reaches 165°F. Drain on a wire rack.

steps.title: Bake waffles
steps.instruction: Cook waffles on a Belgian iron until deep golden, then hold crisp on a rack in a 200°F oven. Do not stack or steam will soften the crust.

steps.title: Plate and serve
steps.instruction: Place one waffle per plate, top with two fried chicken thighs, a knob of maple butter, and a drizzle of hot honey. Serve immediately while chicken skin audibly crunches.

stationWorkflow: Fry chicken in batches while waffles bake—coordinate so both hit the line within 5 minutes.
Hold fried chicken on a wire rack in a 200°F oven, never on paper towels which trap steam.
Whip maple butter ahead and keep hot honey in squeeze bottles for fast finishing at the line.
cleanupNotes: Strain fry oil through a fine mesh once cooled; discard if flour bits are heavily browned.
Wipe waffle iron plates while still warm with a damp cloth—dried batter is stubborn once set.
leftovers: Reheat chicken on a rack at 375°F for 10 minutes to restore crunch; toast waffles separately.
Dice leftover chicken into waffle sandwich sliders with pickles and hot sauce for a quick lunch.
